content_voiceover: This table compares anti-CD38 and anti-CD47 drugs and how each interferes with transfusion testing. Red cell expression, CD47 is expressed at a higher density than CD38. DTT sensitivity, CD38 is destroyed by DTT, but CD47 is not. Common drugs, for anti-CD38 that's daratumumab and isatuximab, for anti-CD47 that's magrolimab and evorpacept. For interference patterns, ABO typing isn't affected by anti-CD38 but reverse typing is affected by anti-CD47. Minor antigen typing requiring anti-human globulin, both interfere. Antibody screening by AHG gel card, both interfere. Antibody screening by manual polybrene, CD38 is not affected, but CD47 is affected. And DTT treatment of red cells removes CD38 interference, but cannot remove CD47 interference. The exam takeaway, DTT and manual polybrene both solve anti-CD38 problems, but neither solves anti-CD47 problems, making anti-CD47 the trickier drug class.
keypoints: CD47 is expressed at higher density on red cells than CD38
DTT destroys CD38 but cannot destroy CD47
Anti-CD47 interferes with ABO reverse typing; anti-CD38 does not
Manual polybrene avoids anti-CD38 interference but not anti-CD47 interference
Anti-CD47 interference cannot be removed by DTT or the MP method
keypoint_voiceover: Key contrast for boards, both anti-CD38 and anti-CD47 interfere with antihuman globulin-based testing, but only anti-CD38, like daratumumab, can be neutralized, either with DTT, since CD38 has disulfide bonds, or by switching to manual polybrene. Anti-CD47 drugs like magrolimab resist both fixes, and anti-CD47 uniquely interferes with ABO reverse typing too.
